subject: ventures/mortgage-extra-payment-vs-invest-calculator
professional: a fee-only CFP (certified financial planner) who answers 'pay down the mortgage or invest' for clients. They would check first: that the amortised payment and payoff month are right, that the three paths spend the same cash, that the break-even return is after-tax and lies above the mortgage rate when gains are taxed, that a recast is modelled as a lower payment over the same term with a fee, and that the limits (risk, liquidity, tax treatment) are stated.

evidence.correctness: Recomputed with an independent Python re-implementation (scratchpad ref.py, written for this audit from the stated model, plus a closed-form check) against calc.mjs run in Node. Defaults (balance 320000, 6.5%, 27 y, 400 extra, 25000 lump, 7% return, 15% gains tax, fee 300): (1) final wealth invest 488,497.46, prepay 484,804.26, recast 484,427.56, identical to the cent in both; the invest path also equals the closed form FV = 25000(1+g)^324 + 400((1+g)^324-1)/g less 15% of gain (488,497.46). (2) Interest paid 359,679.40 / 177,047.51 / 331,579.44, payoff months 324 / 189 / 324 and payments 2,097.78 / 2,497.78 / 1,933.89 match; payment(300000, 6%, 360) = 1,798.65, the textbook figure. (3) Break-even return 6.9443% by my own bisection vs 6.94427% in the tool; above the 6.5% mortgage rate, as it must be when gains are taxed. (4) With return = mortgage rate and no tax or fee all three paths end at 495,124.3587 in both. (5) interestTaxSavingPct 24: invest 763,473.80, prepay 656,211.35 in both. Edge probes: lump 500000 > balance warns and pays off at month 0; return -60 and years 0.04 return warnings, not NaN. Page not loaded in a browser (only its source and page.test.mjs read), so not 4.
evidence.completeness: README claims checked: three-path comparison with after-tax wealth (works), months and interest saved (verified, payoff 189 vs 324 months), break-even return by bisection (works), sensitivity table 2 to 12% (analyze returns 6 rows), CSV export (toCsv, tested for 29 lines), input warnings (works), usage counters and opt-out (usage.test.mjs passes). The 'Not modelled' list (ARMs, escrow, penalties, PMI, liquidity, retirement accounts, dividend tax drag) is honest, and VENTURE.yaml lists a retirement-account option, risk band and printable summary as 'not built'. Stage is prototype and the one hypothesis is untested. Did not drive the rendered page in a browser.
evidence.verification: Ran `node --test calc.test.mjs page.test.mjs usage.test.mjs` in ventures/mortgage-extra-payment-vs-invest-calculator: 28 tests, 28 pass, 0 fail, 0.27 s (calc.test.mjs alone has 15). Four hand-seeded mutations in calc.mjs, each reverted with git checkout (git status clean afterwards). A, `basis += contrib` replaced by `basis += 0` (tax charged on contributions, not just gains): caught, 1 failure. D, bisection direction flipped in breakEvenReturn: caught, 1 failure. B, gains tax scaled by 0.9 (`gain * 0.9`): 15 of 15 pass, NOT caught, because every tax-bearing assertion is an inequality or has 0.5 tolerance with tax set to 0. C, interest tax saving doubled (`/ 100` to `/ 50`): 15 of 15 pass, NOT caught; the only test is `b.rows[0].final > a.rows[0].final`. So the tie-to-the-mortgage-rate property is well guarded, but the tax logic that the 'after tax' headline depends on is pinned by no exact value; no test asserts any dollar figure at the default inputs. Two of four survived: score 2.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (172 lines, whole), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, usage.mjs head, index.html metadata. Good: pure functions, zero dependencies, a header comment that states the model, input cleaning with defaults, explicit refusal of absurd years-left, bisection bracketed with early exits. Defects: clean() silently replaces an unparsable field with the default instead of warning (typing 'abc' as the rate runs a 6.5% loan); a recast with lump 0 still deducts the fee and invests a negative amount at start (inv = -fee) with no warning; analyze() recomputes simulate() three extra times per sensitivity row and 80 bisection steps x 2 simulations, fine at this size; no exported test for the lump > balance recast path values. Acceptable for a senior JS reviewer with those notes.
evidence.claims: Checked: 'nothing leaves the browser' backed by page.test.mjs grep for fetch/XHR/beacon and local-only imports (passes); disclaimer 'No warranty ... not financial advice' present at README.md and index.html:72, and asserted by a test; privacy line and the three usage events match the code (tested); 'return equal to the mortgage rate ... tie' reproduced; break-even and months saved reproduced. Weak: README.md:23 says the paths 'tie to the cent' but the test tolerance is 0.5 dollars (the tie is in fact exact to 1e-4 in my run, so the claim is true but the test does not back it); README says `node --test` runs the tests, which Node 22 rejects as a directory (working: `node --test calc.test.mjs ...`); llms.txt links to the retired duncan-haywood.github.io host; sitemap.xml and robots.txt use relative URLs (`./index.html`, `Sitemap: ./sitemap.xml`), which crawlers ignore, and canonical is `./index.html`; 'Independent of brokers and tax authorities' is unbacked filler. No claim a user would act on was false.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job as a homeowner: enter balance, rate, years left, extra monthly, lump sum, expected return, tax; get three final-wealth numbers, payoff month, interest saved, the break-even return and a sensitivity grid, then download a CSV. The library path produces all of this correctly. First-hour gaps: the 'interest tax saving' is a user-guessed share, with no standard-deduction comparison; no pre-tax retirement-account option (the most common alternative to prepaying); a single constant return with no risk band; a user who types text in a field silently gets defaults. A homeowner can finish the stated job and the page says what it leaves out.
evidence.domain: Compared against the standard amortisation formula (checked to the cent), the usual 'guaranteed return of paying down debt vs expected after-tax return' framing, and standard recast practice (lump to principal, fee, re-amortise over the remaining term). The model matches: fixed rate, equal cash out, break-even above the mortgage rate when gains are taxed, a recast that invests the freed payment. Departures a CFP would flag, all disclosed: flat end-of-period capital gains tax with no dividend drag or loss offset, itemiser benefit as a flat share of interest rather than a marginal-rate, above-standard-deduction calculation, no emergency liquidity or risk pricing, no tax-advantaged account. A planner would use it as a first-pass illustration with those limits.

defects.what: The after-tax headline is guarded by no exact-value test: seeded mutations scaling the gains tax by 0.9 and doubling the interest tax saving both left all 15 calc tests green. A regression in the tax logic would ship, and no test asserts any dollar figure at the default inputs (verified here: invest 488,497.46, prepay 484,804.26, recast 484,427.56, break-even 6.944%).
clean() replaces any unparsable field with its default silently, so a typo in the rate or balance produces a confident result for a loan the user did not describe, with no warning.
A recast with a zero lump sum still pays the fee and starts the investment account at minus the fee, with no warning that there is nothing to recast.
README claims paths 'tie to the cent' while the test tolerance is 0.5 dollars; README says `node --test` runs the suite, which Node 22 rejects as a directory argument.
sitemap.xml, the robots.txt Sitemap line and the canonical link use relative URLs that crawlers ignore, and llms.txt links to the retired github.io host instead of marisstella.app.

verdict: The arithmetic a financial planner checks first is right: an independent Python model and a closed-form check matched all three final-wealth figures, interest paid, payoff months, payments and the 6.944% break-even at the defaults to the cent, the textbook 1,798.65 payment, the rate-equals-return tie, and an itemiser case. The venture is finished for a prototype (completeness 3, limits honestly listed) but does not meet the bar because verification is 2: 28 tests pass, yet seeded bugs that rescaled the gains tax and doubled the interest tax saving both left every test green, so the 'after-tax' result is unpinned. Recheck with `node --test calc.test.mjs page.test.mjs usage.test.mjs` and the sed mutations at calc.mjs `const gain = Math.max(0, inv - basis)` and the `interestTaxSavingPct / 100` line. Small safe fix: add tests asserting the default-input dollar figures above and a tax-saving exact case; make clean() warn on unparsable fields.
